concepts.title: Arrival of Europeans in India
concepts.definition: European powers -- the Portuguese, Dutch, French, and British -- arrived in India from the late 15th century onward, initially for trade and later for territorial control.
concepts.key_idea: The Portuguese arrived first (Vasco da Gama, 1498), followed by the Dutch, British, and French, each establishing trading posts along the Indian coast.
question_patterns: Who was the first European to reach India by sea?
Which European powers came to India for trade?
Where did the Portuguese establish their base in India?
When did the British East India Company arrive in India?
Why did Europeans come to India?

solution_steps.explain: Vasco da Gama of Portugal reached Calicut in 1498.
Portuguese, Dutch, British, and French established trading posts in India.
Europeans came primarily for the spice trade and later for territorial control.

worked_examples.question: Who was the first European to reach India by sea?
worked_examples.solution: Vasco da Gama, a Portuguese explorer, reached Calicut in 1498.

worked_examples.question: Which European powers came to India for trade?
worked_examples.solution: The Portuguese, Dutch, British, and French came to India for trade.

exercises.question: Explain the arrival of European powers in India.

Vasco da Gama reached India in which year?

concepts.title: British East India Company
concepts.definition: The British East India Company, chartered in 1600, was a trading company that gradually acquired political and territorial control over large parts of India.
concepts.key_idea: Starting with trading posts at Surat, Madras, Bombay, and Calcutta, the Company used its commercial privileges to build military and political power.
question_patterns: When was the British East India Company established?
Where were the main British trading posts in India?
How did a trading company become a political power?
What was the significance of the Company's charter?
Name the three presidency cities of the Company.

solution_steps.explain: The British East India Company was chartered in 1600.
Major posts were at Surat, Madras (Fort St. George), Bombay, and Calcutta (Fort William).
Through trade, alliances, and military victories, the Company acquired political control.

worked_examples.question: When was the British East India Company established?
worked_examples.solution: The British East India Company was chartered in 1600 by Queen Elizabeth I.

worked_examples.question: Name the three presidency cities of the Company.
worked_examples.solution: Madras, Bombay, and Calcutta were the three presidency cities.

exercises.question: How did the East India Company become a political power?
Where was the first British factory in India?

concepts.title: Battle of Plassey (1757)
concepts.definition: The Battle of Plassey (1757) was a decisive victory of the British East India Company under Robert Clive over the Nawab of Bengal, Siraj-ud-Daulah, marking the beginning of British political rule in India.
concepts.key_idea: The victory at Plassey gave the Company control over Bengal's revenues and laid the foundation for British political dominance in India.
question_patterns: When and where was the Battle of Plassey fought?
Who won the Battle of Plassey?
Why was the Battle of Plassey important?
Who betrayed Siraj-ud-Daulah at Plassey?
What was the result of the Battle of Plassey?

solution_steps.explain: The Battle of Plassey was fought in 1757 at Plassey in Bengal.
Robert Clive led the British against Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah of Bengal.
The British victory gave them control of Bengal and began British political rule in India.

worked_examples.question: When and where was the Battle of Plassey fought?
worked_examples.solution: The Battle of Plassey was fought in 1757 at Plassey in Bengal.

worked_examples.question: Who betrayed Siraj-ud-Daulah at Plassey?
worked_examples.solution: Mir Jafar, the commander of Siraj-ud-Daulah's army, betrayed him, leading to the British victory.

exercises.question: Explain the significance of the Battle of Plassey.
Who led the British forces at Plassey?
The Battle of Plassey was fought in which year?

concepts.title: Battle of Buxar (1764)
concepts.definition: The Battle of Buxar (1764) was fought between the British East India Company and the combined forces of the Nawabs of Bengal and Awadh and the Mughal Emperor, resulting in a decisive British victory.
concepts.key_idea: The victory at Buxar consolidated British power in Bengal and led to the granting of Diwani (revenue collection rights) of Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa to the Company.
question_patterns: When was the Battle of Buxar fought?
Who fought against the British at Buxar?
What was the significance of the Battle of Buxar?
What is Diwani and who granted it?
How did Buxar differ from Plassey?

solution_steps.explain: In 1764, the British fought the combined armies of Bengal, Awadh, and the Mughal Emperor at Buxar.
The British won decisively, consolidating their hold over Bengal and neighboring regions.
In 1765, the Mughal Emperor granted the Company the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa.

worked_examples.question: When was the Battle of Buxar fought?
worked_examples.solution: The Battle of Buxar was fought in 1764.

worked_examples.question: What was the significance of the Battle of Buxar?
worked_examples.solution: It consolidated British power in Bengal and led to the grant of Diwani rights to the Company.
worked_examples.answer: It secured British control and Diwani rights over Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa.

exercises.question: Explain the significance of the Battle of Buxar.
What was the Diwani?

concepts.title: British Expansion in India
concepts.definition: After Plassey and Buxar, the British East India Company expanded its control across India through wars, subsidiary alliances, and the doctrine of lapse.
concepts.key_idea: The Company used direct conquest, subsidiary alliances (Wellesley), and the doctrine of lapse (Dalhousie) to bring most of India under British control by the mid-19th century.
question_patterns: What was the subsidiary alliance?
Explain the doctrine of lapse.
Who introduced the subsidiary alliance system?
How did the British expand their territory in India?
Which Indian states were annexed under the doctrine of lapse?

solution_steps.explain: Indian rulers had to keep British troops and pay for them, losing independence in foreign policy.
States without a natural heir were annexed by the British under Lord Dalhousie.
Through wars, alliances, and annexation, the Company brought most of India under its control.

worked_examples.question: What was the subsidiary alliance?
worked_examples.solution: It was a system where Indian rulers accepted British troops and paid for their maintenance, surrendering foreign policy control.
worked_examples.answer: A system making Indian rulers dependent on the British.

worked_examples.question: Who introduced the doctrine of lapse?
worked_examples.solution: Lord Dalhousie introduced the doctrine of lapse.

exercises.question: Explain the methods of British expansion in India.

Who introduced the subsidiary alliance system?

concepts.title: Economic Impact of British Rule
concepts.definition: British economic policies transformed India from a producer of manufactured goods into an exporter of raw materials and an importer of British manufactured goods, leading to deindustrialization.
concepts.key_idea: Heavy taxation, unfavorable trade policies, and the destruction of Indian industries led to economic decline and widespread poverty under British rule.
question_patterns: What was the economic impact of British rule on India?
How did British rule affect Indian industries?
Why did Indian handicrafts decline under British rule?
What was the drain of wealth?
How did British trade policies harm India?

solution_steps.explain: British policies destroyed Indian handicrafts by flooding markets with cheap goods.
Surplus revenues were transferred to Britain without adequate return, draining Indian wealth.
India exported raw materials and imported British manufactured goods, harming local industry.

worked_examples.question: What was the economic impact of British rule on India?
worked_examples.solution: British rule led to deindustrialization, the drain of wealth, and widespread poverty in India.
worked_examples.answer: Deindustrialization, drain of wealth, and poverty.

worked_examples.question: What was the drain of wealth?
worked_examples.solution: The drain of wealth referred to the transfer of India's surplus revenues to Britain without fair economic return.
worked_examples.answer: Transfer of Indian wealth to Britain.

exercises.question: Explain the economic impact of British rule in India.
What was the drain of wealth?

concepts.title: Land Revenue Systems
concepts.definition: The British introduced three main land revenue systems -- Zamindari, Ryotwari, and Mahalwari -- to collect taxes from land, each with different implications for farmers and landlords.
concepts.key_idea: The Zamindari system made zamindars the owners who collected revenue; the Ryotwari system settled revenue directly with cultivators; the Mahalwari system collected revenue village by village.
question_patterns: What were the three land revenue systems introduced by the British?
Explain the Zamindari system.
What was the Ryotwari system?
Describe the Mahalwari system.
Which region was under the Zamindari system?

solution_steps.explain: Zamindars collected revenue from peasants and paid fixed amounts to the British; common in Bengal and Bihar.
Revenue was collected directly from individual cultivators (ryots); common in south India.
Revenue was assessed village by village; common in north-western provinces like Punjab and Agra.

worked_examples.question: What were the three land revenue systems introduced by the British?
worked_examples.solution: The three systems were the Zamindari, Ryotwari, and Mahalwari systems.

worked_examples.question: Explain the Zamindari system.
worked_examples.solution: Under the Zamindari system, zamindars were recognized as landowners and collected revenue from peasants on behalf of the British.
worked_examples.answer: Zamindars collected revenue as intermediaries for the British.

exercises.question: Compare the three land revenue systems of British India.
Which region was under the Ryotwari system?

concepts.title: Impact on Indian Industries
concepts.definition: British policies led to the decline of traditional Indian industries, especially textiles, while promoting the export of raw materials and the import of British manufactured goods.
concepts.key_idea: Indian handicrafts, particularly cotton and silk textiles, could not compete with cheap British factory-made goods, leading to the ruin of artisans and deindustrialization.
question_patterns: How did British rule affect Indian industries?
Why did Indian textiles decline under British rule?
What happened to Indian artisans under British rule?
How did British trade policies affect Indian handicrafts?
What was the impact of cheap British goods on Indian industry?

solution_steps.explain: Cheap British manufactured textiles undercut Indian handloom products.
Many artisans lost their livelihood and were forced into agriculture.
India shifted from a manufacturer to a supplier of raw materials like cotton and indigo.

worked_examples.question: How did British rule affect Indian industries?
worked_examples.solution: British policies led to the decline of Indian handicrafts and deindustrialization as cheap British goods flooded the market.

worked_examples.question: Why did Indian textiles decline under British rule?
worked_examples.solution: Indian textiles could not compete with cheap, machine-made British cloth and unfavorable trade policies.
worked_examples.answer: Competition from cheap British manufactured textiles.

exercises.question: Explain the impact of British rule on Indian industries.

concepts.title: Social and Cultural Changes
concepts.definition: British rule brought significant social and cultural changes in India through Western education, social reform movements, and the introduction of new laws and ideas.
concepts.key_idea: Western education, the printing press, and reform movements led by leaders like Raja Ram Mohan Roy challenged social evils and promoted modern ideas of equality and rationalism.
question_patterns: What social changes occurred during British rule?
Who was Raja Ram Mohan Roy?
What was the role of Western education in social reform?
Name two social reform movements of the 19th century.
How did the British introduce modern education in India?

solution_steps.explain: English-medium education and the printing press spread modern ideas across India.
Reformers like Raja Ram Mohan Roy fought practices like sati and promoted women's rights.
New laws banned sati, allowed widow remarriage, and promoted social justice.

worked_examples.question: Who was Raja Ram Mohan Roy?
worked_examples.solution: Raja Ram Mohan Roy was a social reformer who founded the Brahmo Samaj and campaigned against sati.
worked_examples.answer: A social reformer who opposed sati and founded the Brahmo Samaj.

worked_examples.question: What was the role of Western education in social reform?
worked_examples.solution: Western education introduced modern ideas of equality, rationalism, and human rights that fueled reform movements.
worked_examples.answer: It spread modern ideas that inspired social reform.

exercises.question: Discuss the social and cultural changes during British rule.

concepts.title: Resistance to British Rule
concepts.definition: Resistance to British rule took many forms, including tribal uprisings, peasant revolts, civil rebellions, and ultimately the Revolt of 1857, also known as the First War of Independence.
concepts.key_idea: Discontent caused by economic exploitation, social reforms, and political annexations led to widespread resistance, culminating in the Revolt of 1857 which challenged British authority across northern India.
question_patterns: What were the main causes of resistance to British rule?
Describe the Revolt of 1857.
Who were the key leaders of the 1857 revolt?
Why did tribal and peasant uprisings occur?
What was the significance of the Revolt of 1857?

solution_steps.explain: Economic exploitation, annexations, and social reforms angered different sections of society.
It began as a sepoy mutiny and grew into a widespread rebellion across northern India.
The revolt ended Company rule and led to direct British Crown governance of India.

worked_examples.question: What were the main causes of resistance to British rule?
worked_examples.solution: Economic exploitation, political annexations, social reforms, and resentment among soldiers caused resistance.
worked_examples.answer: Economic, political, social, and military causes.

worked_examples.question: Who were the key leaders of the 1857 revolt?
worked_examples.solution: Leaders included Mangal Pandey, Rani Lakshmibai, Bahadur Shah Zafar, Nana Saheb, and Tantia Tope.
worked_examples.answer: Mangal Pandey, Rani Lakshmibai, Bahadur Shah Zafar, Nana Saheb, Tantia Tope
